subject: Dedicated Burst Capacity — GA launch brief (for leadership sync 6/4)
body:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>, Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwoodinference.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwoodinference.com>, Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Jun 3, 2025 at 9:12 AM PT
Subject: Dedicated Burst Capacity — GA launch brief (for leadership sync 6/4)
Attachments: Burst_GA_Launch_Brief_v3.pdf; Burst_GA_Rollout_Checklist_v1.xlsx; Dedicated_Burst_Customer_FAQ_DRAFT.docx

Team — sharing the updated GA launch brief for Dedicated Burst Capacity ahead of the 6/4 leadership sync.

Executive summary
- We’re on track for a staged GA starting week of 6/10, gated by non-burst SLO protection + fleet safety caps.
- Scope is as agreed: in-region bursting only; Redwood-managed shared burst pools by region/hardware; strict guardrails + deterministic admission decisions.
- We have a clear operational plan (dashboards/runbooks/kill-switch) and GTM enablement assets in draft.

GA readiness (what’s done)
- Feature flags and kill-switches are in place (global + per-region/hardware + per-tenant enablement).
- Admission controller + routing integration is in “release candidate” state; fairness enforcement is enabled with anti-starvation protections.
- Metering export is live in staging with idempotency keys on retries; reconciliation checks run daily.
- Observability is complete enough to support GA:
  - burst saturation + denials (by reason)
  - per-tenant burst usage/peaks
  - neighbor impact indicators (p95/p99 latency deltas for non-burst tenants)
- Security/audit logging: burst enable/disable, cap changes, admin overrides are audited; RBAC for support tooling reviewed.

Known risks + mitigations
1) Telemetry lag can cause unfair denials / oscillation
   - Mitigation: smoothing + guard conditions, and the global circuit breaker if telemetry is stale beyond threshold.
   - Rollback: disable burst per region/hardware and/or globally; admission will return deterministic denial codes.

2) Noisy neighbor / non-burst SLO regression
   - Mitigation: fleet safety cap, per-tenant burst ratio limits, cooldown windows, and SLO regression gate that auto-reduces/disables burst.
   - Operational posture: treat any sustained non-burst p95 regression as a rollback trigger during rollout.

3) Billing trust (double counting on retries / reporting discrepancies)
   - Mitigation: idempotent metering on request IDs, reconciliation job, and CS-visible usage export.
   - Customer comms: set expectation that Console usage is near-real-time but billable export is source of truth.

4) Expectation setting: “burst” is capacity above baseline, not guaranteed
   - Mitigation: contract + enablement language explicitly frames burst as best-effort beyond reserved baseline; denial behavior documented with retry guidance.

Rollout proposal (staged)
- Stage 0 (already): internal dogfood + limited beta tenants in us-east.
- Stage 1 (GA start): us-east / H100 burst pool enablement for allowlisted tenants only.
- Stage 2 (expand): us-west / H100 after 7 days of clean SLOs and acceptable denial rates.
- Stage 3 (expand): eu-west / L40S after 10–14 days (dependent on fleet buffer and early-stage learnings).

Gating criteria (per stage)
- Non-burst tenant p95 latency delta: no sustained regression beyond agreed threshold during business hours.
- Burst pool saturation: sustained saturation must not exceed threshold without clear procurement/size action.
- Denial reasons: no elevated “telemetry_stale” or “admission_timeout” class errors.
- Metering reconciliation: within tolerance over 72h.

GTM / enablement
- Sales enablement: one-pager + objection handling (when to recommend burst vs increasing baseline); draft FAQ attached.
- CS readiness: onboarding checklist + escalation path + “how to read denials” guidance.
- Pricing/packaging: final approval needed on price floors + included burst caps per tier.
- Contract language: align on definitions (Baseline vs Burst), limits, and the SLA posture.

Asks for 6/4 leadership sync
1) Confirm staged GA plan + initial region/hardware order.
2) Confirm pricing/packaging guardrails are acceptable for GA (Finance).
3) Confirm contract posture (Legal): best-effort burst + clarity on denials / no implied extra SLA.
4) Confirm GTM enablement timing (Sales/CS): what we can promise in external comms during Stage 1.

References (tracking)
- PM-512 (PRD + launch) / PM-528 (pricing & packaging)
- ENG-4810 (admission controller) / ENG-4848 (gating & rollback) / ENG-4902 (fleet safety cap)
- Support learnings to bake in: SUP-28503 (429s at cap) / SUP-28579 (eu-west admission timeouts)

Please reply with any red flags by EOD today so we can walk into 6/4 with a crisp recommendation.

— Jordan

Subject: Re: Dedicated Burst Capacity — GA launch brief (for leadership sync 6/4)

Looks solid.

Two notes from Product:
- Can we explicitly call out what a customer will see when denied (429 vs queued vs fallback)? In the beta, the “why am I getting 429s?” question came up quickly.
- EU timing: I’m aligned with delaying eu-west/L40S until we see 7 days clean in us-west, but Sales is already asking if we can “promise EU in June.” I’d prefer we frame as “targeting late June pending SLO gates” vs a calendar commitment.

If you want, I can send a short customer messaging paragraph you can paste into the brief.

Lauren Bishop
Product, Dedicated
Redwood Inference

Date: Tue, Jun 3, 2025 at 12:26 PM PT
Subject: Re: Dedicated Burst Capacity — GA launch brief (for leadership sync 6/4)

Finance is good with staged GA with the following conditions (for the leadership readout):

1) Price floors: do not undercut the approved burst $/GPU-sec band without explicit CFO sign-off (especially for “launch deals”).
2) Usage caps: burst must have a configurable tenant-level max ratio and absolute cap (so we can protect downside on long-running batch workloads).
3) Reporting: CS/Sales must have a standard export that matches invoicing (to avoid “Console vs invoice” escalations).

If we align on those, I’m comfortable telling leadership the margin sensitivity is within our approved envelope.

Laura

Date: Tue, Jun 3, 2025 at 1:14 PM PT
Subject: Re: Dedicated Burst Capacity — GA launch brief (for leadership sync 6/4)

Legal view: the brief is directionally correct. Two things I’d like to see explicitly stated for leadership so we don’t create accidental commitments:

- “Burst” is a paid option to access shared Redwood-managed burst pools above Baseline, subject to admission control and safety limits. It is not an additional reserved commitment.
- SLA posture: we should not imply a guarantee of burst availability/latency. Baseline SLA remains; burst is best-effort and can be denied/limited for fleet safety. Denial reasons and expected client behavior (retry/backoff) should be documented.

Also: audit log language is a plus for regulated customers; we should mention retention is per the existing audit log policy (no bespoke retention promises).

Michael Grant
Legal (Commercial)
Redwood Inference

Thanks all — incorporated the feedback into the v3 PDF already attached (and will send v4 if any final changes tonight).

Edits I made based on your notes:
- Added a “Customer experience on denial” section:
  - Immediate denial w/ standardized reason codes when caps/safety gates trip
  - 429 behavior called out explicitly; guidance to backoff + retry with jitter
  - “Fallback” only happens when customer has configured an allowed fallback model/pool (not implicit)
- EU framing: “targeting late June pending SLO gates and fleet buffers” (no calendar promise)
- Finance conditions: added bullets under “Pricing/packaging guardrails” (price floors, tenant caps, invoicing-aligned export)
- Legal language: added one paragraph that burst is best-effort above baseline + no implied additional SLA

Stephanie/Jasmine: if you have a strong preference on the exact wording for the external-facing line (especially around EU timing), send it and I’ll mirror it in the leadership readout.

Next steps:
- I’ll walk leadership through: staged GA recommendation + explicit go/no-go gates + what we can/can’t promise.
- If leadership agrees, we’ll use the checklist (xlsx) as the single-source GA gate doc for the rollout week.

— Jordan
